rationale.conceptual: The method combines classical MD with specialized cluster analysis and a theoretical model (two-parameter model, Tolman correction) to extract structural transition phenomena. It requires understanding the Stillinger cluster definition, ensemble-averaged structure parameter calculation, reference model curves for different fractal dimensionalities, and polynomial fitting to determine the transition temperature. The interplay of simulation and theory is non-trivial.
rationale.execution: The reproduction pipeline involves at least 6 stages: setting up LAMMPS simulations at three temperatures with precise parameters, running long production runs, identifying clusters from trajectories, computing size distributions and structure parameters, constructing reference curves, performing standalone cluster simulations at low temperatures, and finally fitting the reduced structure parameter to extract T₀. Each stage produces intermediate artifacts that feed into the next, and the scale (hundreds of thousands of atoms, tens of ns) demands careful resource management.

The method involves several non-trivial components (cluster identification, structural parameter computation, fractal analysis) and a multi-step pipeline, making both the domain understanding and the engineering orchestration substantial.
